text:
Dina R: heads-up: running into two UX issues with the Go SDK Generator stream API while porting a realtime feature. curious if others have seen this.
Evan L: what are you seeing?
Dina R: first, Stream(ctx) seems to hang if the caller cancels the ctx while Recv() is blocked on network. goroutine sticks around until connection times out (several minutes). second, builder ergonomics: constructing a generator with options is noisy, too many WithX variants. onboarding devs trip on this.
Fiona T: yikes. For the ctx behavior, are you on the new transport that added automatic retry? that can swallow ctx.Done.
Dina R: yep using sdk-go v0.9.2 in sample-app-realtime. here's the simplified snippet from the demo:
```go
ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(context.Background())
stream, err := client.Generator("fast-chat").Stream(ctx, prompt)
if err != nil { return err }
// start reader goroutine
go func() {
  for {
    token, err := stream.Recv()
    if err != nil { log.Printf("recv err: %v", err); return }
    out <- token.Text
  }
}()
// user navigates away -> cancel() is called
cancel()
// expect goroutine to exit quickly but it doesn't
```
Dina R: observed >200 goroutines after users repeatedly open/close sessions. memory climbs.
Evan L: that matches an earlier bug where Read() was not unblocked on ctx cancel. We planned a cancelable reader wrapper that checks ctx in Read() and returns an error. I thought a PR landed for that though.
Fiona T: PR was merged on the js sdk earlier; go didn't get the same work yet. Also, the retry middleware defaults to retry on 429/5xx/401 which is dangerous for streaming. It retries the request and reuses the same stream instance which causes partial-duplicate events.
Dina R: yep saw duplicates when auth refresh happened mid-stream. The UI showed repeated tokens. bad for UX.
Evan L: proposed fixes: 1) add a transport-level cancelable io.Reader that returns ctx.Err() when ctx is Done, 2) disable automatic retries for streaming requests (or make that opt-in), 3) make Stream return a controller object with Close() and a Recv(ctx) variant to be explicit about cancellation.
Dina R: Recv(ctx) would be a nice ergonomic win. current Recv() forces the caller to rely on stream-level ctx only. Recv(ctx) could let callers pass a per-Recv deadline for backpressure.
Fiona T: agreed. API sketch:
```go
stream := client.Generator("x").BuildStream(prompt) // builder returns StreamController
err := stream.Start(ctx)
for {
  tok, err := stream.RecvWith(ctx, time.Second*2)
  if err == context.DeadlineExceeded { // do backpressure handling }
  if err != nil { break }
  fmt.Print(tok.Text)
}
stream.Close()
```
Evan L: implementation notes: RecvWith should select on parsedTokens chan and ctx.Done(). The transport read goroutine should push to parsedTokens but pay attention to ctx. Also we should add tests that assert no goroutine leak after Close/Cancel and simulate token refresh to ensure no duplicate events.
Dina R: sample app idea: tiny example at /examples/go/realtime/streaming-cancel showing proper patterns: Start/Stop, RecvWith, and WithNoRetry flag. That would help reduce onboarding friction — the docs currently show only naive examples.
Fiona T: docs + CHANGELOG entry needed. Also communicate parity with JS/Python: currently those SDKs handle cancel better so people assume Go will behave similarly.
Evan L: I'll open an issue and PR. plan: add WithNoRetry option, implement cancelable reader, introduce RecvWith and StreamController, add example + test. ETA: prototype in 48h.
Dina R: opened issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-go/issues/459 "go stream cancelability + ergonomics" with logs and a small repro harness. @Evan L @Fiona T added.
ops-bot: issue created by Dina R (#459) and assigned to Evan L; label "devex" added.
Fiona T: thanks. let's also add a short troubleshooting note to the quickstart: "If you see goroutine growth when cancelling streams, upgrade to >=0.9.3 and prefer RecvWith or call Close() on StreamController."
Dina R: perfect. i'll follow up with the sample PR and attach the harness for CI. thanks for the quick sync. :raised_hands:
